nodes.name: lem_key_bound
nodes.rationale: Axiomatized Lemma 3.7 (key lemma): E_W[I(W bad) ∑_{U∈𝒰(W)} p^|U|] ≤ 1/3 for q=16p. Flagged: this is an `axiom` (is_axiom), so the statement matches but it is assumed, not proven.

nodes.name: coverCollection
nodes.docstring:
**The genuine cover collection `𝒰(W)`** (paper §3.2): the non-empty
genuine min-tower cover elements `U(W,H)` over `H ∈ ℋ`.
nodes.rationale: The cover collection 𝒰(W) defined at the start of the Proof of Theorem 1.3 (§3.2/§proof).

nodes.name: genuineU
nodes.docstring:
The genuine cover element of `(W, H)`: the biUnion of the fragments of the
minimum tower of `(liftW W, H)`.
nodes.rationale: genuineU(W,H) is the biUnion of the fragments of the minimum tower of (W,H), i.e. U = ⋃_{i=1}^s T_i in the Proof of Theorem 1.3.

nodes.name: liftW
nodes.docstring:
Lift a `Fin s`-indexed sample to a family indexed by `ℕ` (`∅` outside range).
This is `Workspace.Encoding.MinTower.extend`, re-exported for the cover.
nodes.rationale: Plumbing: lifts a `Fin s`-indexed sample tuple to an `ℕ`-indexed family (re-export of MinTower.extend). No paper statement.

nodes.name: liftW_apply_lt
nodes.rationale: Computation lemma for `liftW` on indices below `s`. Pure plumbing.

nodes.name: mem_coverCollection
nodes.rationale: Membership characterization (unfolds the definition of coverCollection). Plumbing.

nodes.name: lambdaH
nodes.docstring: The weight vector λ_H constructed from the fractional cover w.
nodes.rationale: Exactly the weight vector λ_H constructed from the fractional cover w in the Proof of Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: ProbXp
nodes.docstring: The probability of a property `A ⊆ 2^X` under the product measure `X_p`.
nodes.rationale: ProbXp p A = ∑_{S∈A} p^{|S|}(1-p)^{|X|-|S|} is the probability of an event A under the product measure X_p; its single-point form is exactly the paper's P_q(W) = q^{|W|}(1-q)^{|X|-|W|}. Confidence lowered because the paper introduces this measure inline (mostly as P_p(⟨ℋ⟩)) rather than defining the event-probability functional explicitly.

nodes.name: ProbXpJoint
nodes.docstring:
Joint product distribution `X_q^s` evaluated as an expectation:
    `E_{W₁,…,W_s ∼ X_q indep.}[φ W]`.
nodes.rationale: ProbXpJoint q s φ is the expectation E_{W₁,…,W_s ∼ X_q indep.}[φ(W)] of the s-fold product distribution, the object appearing throughout Section 3 (Lemma key, proof of sharp-selector). Linked to the expectation notation; confidence lowered as the paper never gives this functional an explicit definition.

nodes.name: SuffixHalfCond
nodes.docstring:
The half-weight condition for the suffix starting at index `b`:
`2·λ(W ∩ H_{≥b}) ≥ λ(H_{≥b})`.
nodes.rationale: SuffixHalfCond encodes the half-weight condition λ(W∩H') ≥ ½λ(H') for the suffix H_{≥b}, which is the defining inequality of the cutoff b in Definition 3.1.

nodes.name: cutoff
nodes.docstring:
The cutoff index `b(W,H,λ)`: the smallest index with the suffix
half-condition (Definition 3.1).
nodes.rationale: cutoff is b(W,H,λ): the smallest index (via Nat.find) satisfying the suffix half-condition — exactly the integer b of Definition 3.1.

nodes.name: cutoff_spec
nodes.docstring: `cutoff` satisfies the half-condition.

nodes.name: exists_suffixHalfCond

nodes.rationale: Existence of an index satisfying the half-condition, needed to define cutoff via Nat.find. Well-definedness plumbing; the paper asserts existence implicitly.

nodes.name: suffixHalfCond_length
nodes.docstring: The empty suffix (`b = L.length`) always satisfies the half-condition.
nodes.rationale: Establishes that the empty suffix (b = |H|) satisfies the half-condition (0 ≥ 0), the existence fact making the smallest-b well-defined. The paper takes existence of b implicitly; this is plumbing.

`extend` of the restriction of `T` to `Fin s` agrees with `T` on every

**Invariance lemma (task item 1).** For any `T : ℕ → Finset X`, being a tower
of fragments is unchanged by restricting `T` to `Fin s` and re-extending with
`extend`: both sides only read indices `< s`, where `extend (T ∘ Fin.val)`

nodes.name: mem_towerTuples

nodes.name: minTower

nodes.name: minTuple
nodes.docstring: The chosen lex-minimal tower-tuple.
nodes.rationale: The chosen lex-minimal tower-tuple (Fin s indexed), an intermediate before minTower extends it back to ℕ. Construction plumbing.

nodes.name: minTuple_spec
nodes.rationale: Specification (membership + minimality) of minTuple. Plumbing supporting minTower_isTower / minTower_lex_le.

nodes.name: sizeVec
nodes.docstring:
The size vector of a tuple, as an element of `Lex (Fin s → ℕ)`. The
lexicographic `LinearOrder` on `Lex (Fin s → ℕ)` (Mathlib `Pi.Lex.linearOrder`,
since `Fin s` is a finite well-order and `ℕ` is linearly ordered) is exactly the
paper's `⪯` on `ℤ^s` restricted to size vectors.
nodes.rationale: Size vector (|T_1|,…,|T_s|) as an element of Lex (Fin s → ℕ), the carrier of the lex order ⪯. Encoding of the paper's ordering rather than a stated object.

nodes.name: tFeasible_congr
nodes.docstring:
`TFeasible` only reads indices `< s` of `Z` and `t`: if two pairs `(Z,t)` and
`(Z',t')` agree on `[0,s)` then the `TFeasible` predicate is the same.
nodes.rationale: TFeasible depends only on indices < s. Congruence/well-definedness plumbing.

nodes.name: towerTuples
nodes.docstring:
The finite set of tower-tuples: tuples `T : Fin s → Finset X` whose every
entry is a subset of `H` and whose `extend` is a tower of fragments of `(W,H)`.
Filtering uses `Classical.dec` for the (undecidable) `IsTowerOfFragments`
predicate, which is fine under `open Classical`.
nodes.rationale: The finite set of admissible tower-tuples (subsets of H whose extend is a tower of fragments). Construction infrastructure to take the finite argmin; not a paper object.

nodes.name: towerTuples_nonempty
nodes.docstring:
`towerTuples` is nonempty: the restriction to `Fin s` of Lemma 3.5's witness
`fun i => Rstep W H lambda i \ W i` is a tower-tuple — each value is `⊆ H`, and
its `extend` is a tower of fragments by the invariance lemma.
nodes.rationale: Nonemptiness of the set of tower-tuples: the explicit witness T_i = R_i(W,H) \ W_i is a tower of fragments, which is exactly the one-line proof the paper gives for existence of a tower of fragments.

nodes.name: Hstep_disjoint_biUnion
nodes.docstring: `Hstep j` is disjoint from `⋃_{i<j} Wᵢ`. (No `Rstep ⊆ W` premise needed.)
nodes.rationale: Hstep j disjoint from ⋃_{i<j} W_i (the paper notes Ĥ_{j+1} is disjoint from ⋃ W_i). Disjointness plumbing supporting the halving induction.

nodes.name: Hstep_eq_sdiff_biUnion
nodes.docstring: **`Hstep j = H ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Wᵢ`**, given `Rstep i ⊆ Wᵢ` for all `i < j`.
nodes.rationale: Hstep j = H \ ⋃_{i<j} W_i under Rstep ⊆ W. Set-identity plumbing for the induction.

nodes.name: Rset_union_geSet
nodes.docstring: `Rset ∪ geSet = H`: the cutoff prefix and suffix together recover `H`.
nodes.rationale: Set identity Rset ∪ geSet = H (prefix/suffix partition of H at the cutoff). Plumbing; no stated paper counterpart.

nodes.name: bad_implies_nonempty_tower
nodes.docstring:
**Lemma 3.8.** If `W` is bad, then every tower of fragments `T` of `(W,H)`
(for `H ∈ ℋ`) is nonempty: `∑_{i<s} |Tᵢ| > 0`.
nodes.rationale: Direct formalization of the (unnumbered) lemma in §3.3: a bad W forces every tower of fragments of (W,H) to be nonempty, ∑_{i<s}|T_i| > 0.

nodes.name: geSet_eq_sdiff_Rset
nodes.docstring: `geSet = H ∖ Rset` (prefix/suffix complementarity).
nodes.rationale: geSet = H \ Rset, prefix/suffix complementarity. Set-algebra plumbing.

nodes.name: geSet_half_weight
nodes.docstring:
**Half-weight of the cutoff suffix** (`cutoff_spec`, re-expressed):
`λ((H)_{≥ b̂}) ≤ 2 · λ(Ŵ ∩ (H)_{≥ b̂})`.
nodes.rationale: Half-weight of the cutoff suffix: λ((H)_{≥b}) ≤ 2·λ(W ∩ (H)_{≥b}), i.e. λ(W ∩ H') ≥ ½ λ(H') from the cutoff Definition of b. Low confidence: re-expression of the cutoff defining inequality.

nodes.name: sdiff_biUnion_subset_Hstep
nodes.docstring: `H ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Wᵢ ⊆ Hstep j`, given `Rstep i ⊆ Wᵢ` for all `i < j`.
nodes.rationale: H \ ⋃_{i<j} W_i ⊆ Hstep j under Rstep ⊆ W. Set-inclusion plumbing for the induction.

nodes.name: wt_Hstep_le
nodes.docstring: **The halving induction**: `λ(Hstep j) ≤ 2^{−j} · λ(H)` for all `j`.
nodes.rationale: The halving induction λ(Hstep j) ≤ 2^{-j} λ(H), which is exactly the inductive claim λ_{Ĥ}(Ĥ \ ⋃_{i≤j} W_i) ≤ 2^{-j} λ_{Ĥ}(Ĥ) proved inside the nonempty-tower lemma.

nodes.name: wt_Hstep_succ_le_half
nodes.docstring:
One halving step of the induction:
`λ(Hstep (j+1)) ≤ ½ · λ(Hstep j)`.
nodes.rationale: Single halving step λ(Hstep (j+1)) ≤ ½ λ(Hstep j), the inductive step inequality in the proof of the nonempty-tower lemma. Low confidence: an internal step.

nodes.name: Hstep
nodes.docstring: The iterated finset `Hᵢ`: `Hstep 0 = H`, `Hstep (i+1) = (Hstep i)_{≥} ∖ Wᵢ`.
nodes.rationale: Hstep is the iterated finset H_i from the procedure: Hstep 0 = H and Hstep (i+1) = (H_i)_{>=b_i} \ W_i, exactly the paper's recursion H_1 = H, H_{i+1} = (H_i)_{>=b_i} \ W_i (under the stated 0-based index shift).

nodes.name: Hstep_antitone
nodes.docstring: Monotone decreasing: for `i ≤ j`, `Hⱼ ⊆ Hᵢ`.
nodes.rationale: For i <= j, H_j subseteq H_i. Monotonicity plumbing for the iteration.

nodes.name: Hstep_succ
nodes.rationale: Definitional unfolding of the successor step Hstep (i+1) = geSet ... \ W i. Simp plumbing.

nodes.docstring: One step shrinks all the way: `Hᵢ₊₁ ⊆ Hᵢ`.
nodes.rationale: H_{i+1} subseteq H_i. Monotonicity plumbing for the iteration.

nodes.docstring: One step shrinks: `Hᵢ₊₁ ⊆ (Hᵢ)_{≥}`.
nodes.rationale: H_{i+1} subseteq (H_i)_{>=}. Monotonicity plumbing for the iteration.

nodes.rationale: Rset is the cutoff prefix H_{<b} = (H_i)_{<b_i}, which is the paper's R_i(W,H). Defined as the take-prefix of the canonical enumeration up to b.

nodes.name: Rset_disjoint_geSet
nodes.docstring: `Rset` (the cutoff prefix) is disjoint from `geSet` (the cutoff suffix).
nodes.rationale: Rset (cutoff prefix) disjoint from geSet (cutoff suffix). Follows from H_{<b} = H \ H_{>=b}; structural plumbing, not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: Rset_subset
nodes.docstring: `Rset` is a subset of `H`.
nodes.rationale: Rset subseteq H. Trivial containment of the prefix; plumbing.

nodes.name: Rstep
nodes.docstring:
The cutoff prefix at step `i`: `Rstep i = (Hᵢ)_{< bᵢ}` (the paper's `R_{i+1}`
under the indexing note above).
nodes.rationale: Rstep is the per-step cutoff prefix R_i(W,H) = (H_i)_{<b_i} from the procedure.

nodes.name: Rstep_subset_Hstep
nodes.docstring: `Rstep i ⊆ Hᵢ`.
nodes.rationale: R_i subseteq H_i. Containment plumbing.

nodes.docstring:
The cutoff index `bᵢ = b(W, H, λ)` (Definition 3.1), via the canonical
enumeration.

Definition 3.1 is kept as Lemma32.SuffixHalfCond (the half-weight inequality) + Lemma32.cutoff (the smallest-index Nat.find definition).

nodes.docstring: The descending-by-`λ` ordering relation on `X`.
nodes.rationale: The descending-by-lambda ordering relation used to build a canonical enumeration of H. Plumbing for the paper's phrase 'order the elements of H as h_1,...,h_{|H|} such that lambda(h_1) >= ... >= lambda(h_{|H|})'; not itself a paper statement.

nodes.rationale: geSet subseteq H. Trivial containment of the suffix; plumbing.

nodes.docstring: Canonical descending enumeration of `H` by `λ`.
nodes.rationale: Canonical descending enumeration of H by lambda (mergeSort). Realizes the paper's element ordering h_1 >= ... >= h_{|H|} from Definition 3.1; an implementation choice, not a stated result.

nodes.name: sortedOf_nodup
nodes.docstring: `sortedOf` is duplicate-free.
nodes.rationale: sortedOf is duplicate-free. Plumbing about the canonical enumeration.

nodes.rationale: sortedOf is a permutation of H.toList. Plumbing about the canonical enumeration.

nodes.rationale: sortedOf enumerates exactly H. Plumbing about the canonical enumeration.

nodes.rationale: Prefix and suffix of a nodup list are disjoint as finsets. Generic list lemma; plumbing.

nodes.name: IsTowerOfFragments
nodes.docstring:
**Definition 3.4 (towers of fragments).**

Given a sample family `W : ℕ → Finset X` and a hypothesis `H` (the paper takes
`H ∈ ℋ`; we expose this predicate without baking in `H ∈ ℋ` — the existence lemma
supplies `H ∈ ℋ`, and the `TFeasible` witness range over `ℋ` carries the membership
requirement where the paper needs it), a tuple `T : ℕ → Finset X` is a *tower of
fragments* of `(W,H)` iff:

* (feasibility) `Z := fun i => T i ∪ W i` is `t`-feasible for `t := fun i => (T i).card`,
* (containment) `∀ i < s, T i ⊆ H` (the paper's `⋃_i T_i ⊆ H`), and
* (disjointness) `∀ i < s, Disjoint (T i) (W i)` (needed for the surjection recovery `W_i = Z_i ∖ T_i`).
nodes.rationale: Formalizes Definition 3.4 (tower of fragments): Z_i = T_i cup W_i is t-feasible for t_i = |T_i|, and union T_i subseteq H (the per-index T_i subseteq H is the Lean form of union T_i subseteq H). The extra Disjoint (T_i) (W_i) clause is the recovery condition W_i = Z_i \ T_i made explicit.

nodes.name: TFeasible
nodes.docstring:
**Definition 3.3 (`def:feas`, `t`-feasibility).**

A tuple `Z : ℕ → Finset X` is `t`-feasible (for `t : ℕ → ℕ`) with respect to the
hypothesis family `ℋ : Set (Finset X)`, sample bound `s`, and the *family* of
weights `lambda_vec : (H : Finset X) → H ∈ ℋ → X → ℝ` (one `λ_H` per `H ∈ ℋ`),
iff there exist a witness family `W' : ℕ → Finset X` and `H ∈ ℋ` (with membership
witness `hH`) such that for all `i < s`:

* `W' i ⊆ Z i`,
* `(W' i).card = (Z i).card - t i`, and
* `Rstep W' H (lambda_vec H hH) i ⊆ Z i` (i.e. `R_i(W',H) ⊆ Z_i`), where the
  procedure for the witness `H` uses *its own* weight `λ_H = lambda_vec H hH`.

The cutoff tuple `b = b(W',H)` of the paper is implicit in `Rstep` (each
`Rstep W' H lambda i = (H_i)_{<b_i}` uses `b_i = bIdx (W' i) (Hstep W' H λ i) λ`),
so it is not quantified separately — see the file header.
nodes.rationale: Formalizes Definition 3.3 (def:feas) t-feasibility: there exist a witness W' and H in H with |W'_i| = |Z_i| - t_i, W'_i subseteq Z_i, and R_i(W',H) subseteq Z_i for all i < s. The existential over b is absorbed into Rstep (b is a deterministic function of (W',H)), as the file header documents.

nodes.name: exists_tower_of_fragments
nodes.docstring:
**Lemma 3.5 (a tower of fragments exists).**

For any `W : ℕ → Finset X` and `H ∈ ℋ`, the tuple
`Tstar i = Rstep W H (lambda_vec H hH) i \ W i` (using `H`'s own weight `λ_H`) is a
tower of fragments of `(W,H)`.

This is the paper's "simple observation that `T` with `T_i = R_i(W,H) ∖ W_i` is a
tower of fragments of `(W,H)`".
nodes.rationale: Formalizes Lemma 3.5 ('For any H and W, there exists a tower of fragments of (W,H)'), proved exactly by the paper's witness T_i = R_i(W,H) \ W_i. The Lean statement constructs that explicit tower; the span quotes the proof's defining observation (the lemma statement itself has no \label, so the witness sentence is the most specific verbatim anchor).

nodes.name: bernoulli_ineq
nodes.docstring:
Bernoulli-style upper bound:
For `0 ≤ q ≤ 1` and `s : ℕ`, we have `1 - (1 - q)^s ≤ s · q`.

This is the standard form of Bernoulli's inequality `(1 - q)^s ≥ 1 - s·q`,
rewritten as an upper bound on `1 - (1-q)^s`.

The hypothesis `q ≤ 1` is essential: for `q > 1` the inequality fails
(e.g., `q = 4, s = 3` gives `1 - (-3)^3 = 28` and `s·q = 12`).
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the inequality 1 - (1-q)^s <= s*q (Bernoulli), which is exactly the bound tilde{q} = 1 - (1-q)^s <= sq used in the proof of Theorem 1.2 to relate the union of s samples to a single sample of density sq. Confidence < 1 because in Lean it is a standalone arithmetic lemma; in the paper it is an inline assertion.

nodes.name: c_sel_fact
nodes.rationale: Pure numeric fact 1 ≤ 100·log 2, used to validate the concrete constant choice (c_sel ≤ 100·log 2) in the formalization's instantiation of the absolute constant c. The specific value 100·log 2 does not appear in the paper, which only asserts existence of an absolute constant; this is constant-bookkeeping plumbing.

nodes.name: cover_bound_of_not_psmall
nodes.docstring:
**Cover bound from "not p-small"** (paper §3.3, the inequality
`∑_{U ∈ 𝒰(W)} p^|U| ≥ 1/2` whenever `𝒰(W)` is a cover of `ℋ`).

Statement (informal): if `ℋ` is *not* `p`-small, then for every cover
`𝒰` of `ℋ` (i.e. every `H ∈ ℋ` has some `U ∈ 𝒰` with `U ⊆ H`), we have
`∑_{U ∈ 𝒰} p^{|U|} ≥ 1/2`.

In the present formalisation, we expose this as a generic fact about
covers `g : Finset X → Bool` of `ℋ`. By definition of `IsPSmall`, the
*negation* says: for every integral cover `g`, the cost
`∑_W (if g W then 1 else 0) * p^|W|` is `> 1/2`. This is what we
package here.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 3.3, "Conclusion" paragraph)
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the fact that any (integral) cover U of ℋ that is not p-small has ∑_{U∈𝒰} p^|U| > 1/2 — the contrapositive of IsPSmall — which the paper invokes as 'any cover 𝒰 for ℋ must have ∑ p^|U| ≥ 1/2'. Used to convert the bad-cover bound into a probability bound.

nodes.name: exp_bound
nodes.docstring:
exp_bound theorem: expectation lower bound.

    If with probability at least 1/3 (under the product measure X_{q'}) there exists
    H ∈ ℋ with ∑_{W' ⊆ H ∩ W} w(W') ≥ 1/2, then E_{W ~ X_{q'}}[∑_{W' ⊆ W} w(W')] ≥ 1/6.

    By linearity of expectation (`expectation_eq_sum`), the RHS equals
    ∑_W w(W) q'^|W|, giving the stated bound.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: exp_bound concludes 1/6 ≤ ∑_W w(W) (q')^{|W|} = E[∑_{W⊆X_{q'}} w(W)] from the probability-≥1/3 good event; this is the expectation lower-bound step in the Proof of Theorem 1.1 (the chain E[...] ≥ 1/6 combined with the linearity-of-expectation identity quoted).

nodes.name: expectation_eq_sum
nodes.docstring:
The expectation of ∑_W w(W) q'^|W| equals ∑_W w(W) q'^|W| by linearity.
    This is a standard fact from linearity of expectation.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the linearity-of-expectation identity E[ sum_{W subseteq X_{q'}} w(W) ] = sum_W w(W) (q')^|W| in the proof of Theorem 1.1. The Lean statement expands the expectation over the Bernoulli product measure q'^|W| (1-q')^(|X|-|W|), giving exactly this equation.

nodes.name: expectation_lower_bound
nodes.docstring:
If an event has probability at least p and the random variable is at least v on that event,
    then the expectation is at least p * v. This is a standard probability fact.

    The hypothesis `h_Z_nonneg : ∀ W, 0 ≤ Z W` is required: without it the statement is false
    (a large negative `Z` outside `A` can drive the RHS arbitrarily negative). In the intended
    application (`exp_bound`), `Z(W) = ∑_{W' ⊆ W} cov.w W' ≥ 0`, so the hypothesis is satisfied.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Generic Markov-type bound E[Z] ≥ p·v when P(A) ≥ p, Z ≥ v on A, Z ≥ 0. In the proof of Theorem 1.2 this is the step that turns 'with probability at least 1/3 the quantity is ≥ 1/2' into 'its expectation ≥ 1/6'. nodes.name: heavy_le
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem: heavy_le**
For s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉, we have 1 - 2^(-s) ≥ 1 - 1/(2t).

**Mathematical Proof**:
- The inequality 1 - 2^(-s) ≥ 1 - 1/(2t) is equivalent to 2^(-s) ≤ 1/(2t)
- Which is equivalent to 2^s ≥ 2t
- Taking log₂: s ≥ log₂(2t)
- This holds by the ceiling property: ⌈x⌉ ≥ x

**Implementation Note**: The mathematical argument is straightforward:
1. s = ⌈log(2t) / log(2)⌉ ≥ log(2t) / log(2) (by ceiling property)
2. Multiply by log(2) > 0: s * log(2) ≥ log(2t)
3. Take exp: 2^s ≥ 2t
4. Take reciprocals: 1/2^s ≤ 1/(2t)
5. Therefore: 1 - 1/2^s ≥ 1 - 1/(2t)

This requires finding the correct lemmas for inverse inequalities and combining
logarithm/exponential properties. The proof is doable but requires careful
application of Mathlib lemmas.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic step in the Proof of Theorem 1.1: for s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉ the Theorem-1.3 guarantee 1−2^{−s} upgrades to the bound 1 − 1/(2t) used in the displayed inequality.

The Bernoulli weight `∏_i q^|W_i|·(1-q)^(|X|-|W_i|)` is non-negative
when `q ∈ [0,1]`.

nodes.name: prob_xp_joint_norm
nodes.docstring:
Normalisation: the joint distribution sums to 1 over the constant function 1.

Proof:
* Swap `∑ W : Fin s → Finset X, ∏ i, ...` to `∏ i, ∑ S : Finset X, ...` via
  `Finset.sum_prod_piFinset` (after converting `Finset.univ` over functions to
  `Fintype.piFinset` of pointwise `Finset.univ`).
* Each inner sum equals `(q + (1-q))^(card X) = 1` by `Fintype.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow`.
* The outer product over `Fin s` of `1`'s is `1`.
nodes.rationale: The joint distribution is a probability measure: it sums to 1 over the constant function 1. Normalization plumbing; the paper treats X_q^s as a probability measure implicitly.

nodes.name: IsBad
nodes.docstring: The "bad" predicate on a tuple of samples `W : Fin s → Finset X`.

nodes.name: coverCollection_witness
nodes.docstring:
For each non-empty `H ∈ ℋ` and *bad* `W`, the genuine min-tower cover
element `U := genuineU ℋ s lambda_vec W H hH = ⋃_{i<s} minTower(liftW W, H)_i`
lies in `coverCollection ℋ s lambda_vec W` and is a subset of `H`.

Non-emptiness `1 ≤ |U|` is paper Lemma 3.8 (`bad_implies_nonempty_tower`): a bad
`W` has a non-empty tower. Containment `U ⊆ H` is the tower-of-fragments
containment (`minTower_isTower`).
nodes.rationale: For each non-empty H and bad W there is U ∈ 𝒰(W) with U ⊆ H — the Lean form of the Claim that 𝒰(W) covers ℋ (combined with non-emptiness for bad W).

nodes.name: coverCost
nodes.docstring: The cover cost `∑_{U ∈ 𝒰(W)} p^|U|`.
nodes.rationale: coverCost is the cover cost ∑_{U∈𝒰(W)} p^{|U|} appearing throughout the Proof of Theorem 1.3 and Lemma key.

nodes.name: coverCost_gt_half_of_not_psmall
nodes.docstring:
**Cover bound** (proven from `cover_bound_of_not_psmall`):
for `¬ IsPSmall ℋ p` and *bad* `W`, we have `coverCost ℋ s lambda_vec p W > 1/2`.
nodes.rationale: For not-p-small ℋ and bad W, coverCost > 1/2 — exactly the fact that any cover of ℋ costs at least 1/2 (the lower bound used to bound P[bad]).

nodes.name: coverFromCollection
nodes.docstring:
The IntegralCover constructed from `coverCollection W`, valid only when
`W` is *bad* (so that `coverCollection_witness` produces a non-empty `U`
for each `H ∈ ℋ`).
nodes.rationale: Packages coverCollection as an IntegralCover structure for bad W. Constructive plumbing; the paper does not name this object.

nodes.name: key_lemma_bound
nodes.docstring:
**`key_lemma_bound`** — `Pr[bad] ≤ 2/3` for `q = 16p` and not-`p`-small `ℋ`.

# Proof (paper §3.3)

1. **Cover bound** (`coverCost_gt_half_of_not_psmall`, proven):
   For any `W`, `coverCost ℋ s lambda_vec p W > 1/2`. In particular,
   `(1/2) · I[bad] ≤ I[bad] · coverCost`. Integrating:
   `(1/2) · Pr[bad] ≤ E[I[bad] · coverCost]`.

2. **Surjection bound** (`expectation_bound_via_surjection`, axiom):
   `E[I[bad] · coverCost] ≤ ∑_{u≥1} C(2u, u) · ((1-q)·p/q)^u`.

3. **Termwise bound** (`central_binomial_bound`, proven):
   `C(2u, u) · ((1-q)·p/q)^u ≤ (1/4)^u` for `q = 16p`.

4. **Geometric series** (`geometric_series_quarter`, proven):
   `∑_{u≥1} (1/4)^u = 1/3`.

5. **Combine**: `(1/2) · Pr[bad] ≤ 1/3`, hence `Pr[bad] ≤ 2/3`.
nodes.rationale: P[W bad] ≤ 2/3, the consequence of Lemma key combined with the not-p-small lower bound, in the Proof of Theorem 1.3.

nodes.name: lambdaH_sum_eq_w_relation
nodes.docstring:
Auxiliary lemma: the sum of λ_H over W ∩ H relates to the fractional cover w.
    This is equation (4.2) in the paper proof.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the first equality in the displayed computation of sum_{x in X_{q'} cap H} lambda_H(x) in the proof of Theorem 1.1, expressing the partial sum of lambda_H over W cap H as (sum w(W) - correction) / (sum w(W)). The Lean term-for-term mirrors that ratio (W playing the role of X_{q'}).

nodes.name: lambdaH_to_w_inequality
nodes.docstring:
The key inequality relating λ_H to w.
    When λ_H is heavy on W ∩ H, then w is heavy on subsets of H ∩ W.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Given λ_H heavy on W∩H (∑ λ_H ≥ 1 − 1/(2t)), this derives ∑_{W'⊆H∩W} w(W') ≥ 1/2. It realizes exactly the displayed step in the proof of Theorem 1.2 that turns max_H ∑ λ_H ≥ 1 − 1/(2t) into max_H ∑_{W⊆H∩X_{q'}} w(W) ≥ 1/2, via the chain bounding ∑_{x∈X_{q'}∩H} λ_H(x).

nodes.name: term_bound
nodes.docstring:
Term-by-term bound used in the proof of `lambdaH_to_w_inequality`.

For any `W' : Finset X` and any `W : Finset X`, under the support condition
`h_supp` (`cov.w W' = 0` for `|W'| > t`) and `1 ≤ t`, we have:

  (if W' ⊆ W then 0 else cov.w W') / t
    ≤ (if W' ⊆ W then 0 else cov.w W' * ((W'.card - (W' ∩ W).card) / W'.card))

The intuition: when `W' ⊄ W`, there is at least one element of `W'` outside `W`,
so `|W' ∩ W| ≤ |W'| - 1`, hence `(|W'| - |W' ∩ W|)/|W'| ≥ 1/|W'| ≥ 1/t`
(the last using `cov.w W' > 0 ⇒ |W'| ≤ t`).

This lemma is broken out as a helper to keep the main proof readable.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-term inequality (for W' ⊄ W: w(W')/t ≤ w(W')·(|W'|-|W'∩W|)/|W'|) underlying the first inequality in the displayed bound for ∑_{x∈X_q'∩H} λ_H(x), which the paper justifies by '|W| ≤ t for all W ∈ 𝒲'. Low confidence: an internal proof step, not a stated result.

nodes.name: lambdaH_denom_eq
nodes.docstring:
Helper: rewrite the denominator as ∑_{W ⊆ H} w(W).

Proof strategy: Exchange order of summation, then for each W ⊆ H:
∑_{y ∈ H} (if y ∈ W then w(W)/|W| else 0) = ∑_{y ∈ W} w(W)/|W| = w(W).

The equality ∑_{y ∈ W} w(W)/|W| = w(W) follows from:
- ∑_{y ∈ W} w(W)/|W| = |W| · (w(W)/|W|) = w(W) when |W| > 0
- Both sides are 0 when W = ∅ (by w_empty)

This is mathematically straightforward but requires library work for sum exchange.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: Exactly the denominator identity displayed in the Proof of Theorem 1.1 (∑_y ∑_{W∋y,W⊆H} w(W)/|W| = ∑_{W⊆H} w(W)).

nodes.name: lambdaH_denom_pos
nodes.docstring:
The denominator of λ_H is positive when H is covered.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf

The paper uses lambda_H as a well-defined weight vector but never states denominator-positivity as a result; it is an auxiliary fact needed to make the Lean division of lambda_H meaningful.

nodes.docstring:
Theorem: λ_H(x) ≤ 1 for all x.

Proof strategy: The numerator for x only includes W with x ∈ W, while
the denominator includes all W ⊆ H. So numerator ≤ denominator.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)

This is a well-definedness/range property confirming λ_H : X → [0,1] (a hypothesis of Theorem 1.1 when λ_H is fed in); the paper does not state it as a result — it follows immediately from the explicit formula. Plumbing about the λ_H definition.

nodes.docstring:
Theorem: λ_H(x) is non-negative.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)

The paper only requires λ_H : X → [0,1]; it does not state nonnegativity as a separate result. Plumbing to discharge the selector theorem's hypothesis on λ_H.

The numerator of λ_H(x) is non-negative.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf

nodes.name: lambdaH_num_sum_eq_denom
nodes.docstring:
Helper: Sum of numerators over all x equals the denominator.

For each W ⊆ H, the contribution to the sum is:
∑_{x ∈ X} ∑_{W ∋ x} w(W)/|W| = ∑_W (∑_{x ∈ W} w(W)/|W|) = ∑_W w(W).

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)

It is NOT the displayed denominator identity on line 549 (sum_{y in H} ... = sum_{W subseteq H} w(W)), which is exactly captured by lambdaH_denom_eq. Demoted to helper to avoid over-linking the same display.

nodes.name: lambdaH_num_zero_of_not_mem

Helper: the numerator is 0 when x is not in H.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)

nodes.name: lambdaH_sum_one
nodes.docstring:
Theorem: ∑_{x ∈ X} λ_H(x) = 1.

Proof strategy:
- Numerator sum: ∑_x ∑_W (if x ∈ W then w(W)/|W| else 0)
- After exchange: ∑_W ∑_{x ∈ W} w(W)/|W| = ∑_W w(W)
- This equals the denominator
- Therefore the ratio is 1

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)

Theorem: λ_H(x) = 0 when x ∉ H.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)

nodes.name: max_w_prob
nodes.docstring:
max_w_prob theorem: probability bound conversion from λ_H to w.

    Given a probability lower bound on the heavy-λ event, we transfer it to a
    probability lower bound on the heavy-w event. The transformation goes through
    a deterministic set inclusion (via `lambdaH_to_w_inequality`) and uses
    set monotonicity of `ProbXp`.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Transfers the with-probability-1/3 heavy-lambda event (max_H sum lambda_H >= 1 - 2^{-s}) to the with-probability-1/3 heavy-w event (max_H sum_{W subseteq H cap X_{q'}} w(W) >= 1/2) in the proof of Theorem 1.1, via the deterministic inclusion lambdaH_to_w_inequality plus monotonicity of ProbXp. Confidence < 1: it is the probabilistic step deriving this displayed line, not a numbered theorem.

nodes.name: s_pos
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem: s_pos**
For t ≥ 2, we have s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉ > 0.

**Mathematical Proof**:
- For t ≥ 2, we have 2t ≥ 4
- Since log₂ is strictly increasing and log₂(4) = 2
- We get log₂(2t) ≥ 2
- By ceiling property: s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉ ≥ log₂(2t) ≥ 2 > 0

**Implementation Note**: This theorem requires:
1. log₂(x) = log(x) / log(2) in Lean
2. Properties: log is strictly increasing for x > 0
3. log(4) / log(2) = 2 (computable)
4. Ceiling function properties: ⌈x⌉ ≥ x
These are available in Mathlib but require careful chaining of lemmas.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: For t ≥ 2, the iteration count s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉ is positive. Parameter/well-definedness plumbing: the formalization picks s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉ to instantiate Theorem 1.1 (where 1−2^{-s} ≥ 1−1/(2t)); the positivity of this choice is not a stated paper result.

nodes.name: pow_bound_from_ratio
nodes.docstring:
If 0 ≤ q' ≤ p/6 and W.card ≥ 1, then q'^|W| ≤ (p/6)^|W| ≤ (1/6) p^|W|.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: Per-term algebraic step q'^k ≤ (1/6)·p^k for q' ≤ p/6, k ≥ 1, which is exactly the inequality (q')^|W| ≤ (p/6)^|W| underlying the displayed bound E[∑ w(W)] ≤ ∑ (p/6)^|W| w(W) in the proof of Theorem 1.1. Low confidence: a supporting arithmetic step, not a stated result.

nodes.name: prob_good_event
nodes.docstring:
**`prob_good_event` (Theorem 1.3 deep content, paper Section 3.3).**

For `q = 16p`, if `ℋ` is *not* `p`-small and `λ_H : X → [0,1]` is any family
of weight vectors, then
`1/3 ≤ ProbXp (1 - (1-q)^s) {W : ∃ H ∈ ℋ, 1 - 2^{-s} ≤ ∑_{x ∈ W} λ_H(x)}`.

# Proof structure

Following the paper Section 3.3:

1. **Bad event**: `W = (W_1,…,W_s)` is *bad* iff `∀ H ∈ ℋ`,
   `∑_{x ∈ ⋃W_i ∩ H} λ_H(x) < 1 - 2^{-s}`.

2. **`Lemma_KeyLemma.key_lemma_bound`** gives `Pr_{joint}[bad] ≤ 2/3`
   (the deep content of paper §3.3, now admitted as the single
   `¬IsPSmall ℋ p`-scoped bound axiom `Workspace.Axioms.LemKey.lem_key_bound`
   — the paper's `lem:key` bound).

3. **`Lemma_JointProbBasics.prob_xp_joint_complement`** gives
   `Pr[¬bad] = 1 - Pr[bad] ≥ 1/3` (uses `prob_xp_joint_norm`, which is
   the discrete Bernoulli normalisation identity, fully proven).

4. **"Not bad ⇒ heavy"**: if `W` is not bad, some `H` witnesses
   `1 - 2^{-s} ≤ ∑_{x ∈ ⋃W_i ∩ H} λ_H ≤ ∑_{x ∈ ⋃W_i} λ_H` (since `λ_H ≥ 0`),
   so `⋃W_i` lies in the heavy event.

5. **`Lemma_JointProbBasics.prob_xp_joint_mono`** lifts the pointwise
   inequality `I[¬bad] ≤ I[(⋃W_i) ∈ heavy]` to the joint expectation.

6. **`Lemma_UnionDistribution.union_distribution_eq`** gives
   `Pr_{joint}[(⋃W_i) ∈ A] = ProbXp (1 - (1-q)^s) A` (fully proven).

7. **Conclude**: combine the chain to land in `1/3 ≤ ProbXp (1-(1-q)^s) heavy`.

# Status

The remaining external assumption is exactly the single minimal
`¬IsPSmall ℋ p`-scoped bound axiom `Workspace.Axioms.LemKey.lem_key_bound`
(the paper's §3.3 `lem:key` bound).

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 3.3, eqs. 3.6 and surrounding)
nodes.rationale: Conclusion `1/3 ≤ ProbXp(1-(1-q)^s){W | ∃H, 1-2^{-s} ≤ ∑_{x∈W} λ_H(x)}` is exactly the final displayed probability bound completing the Proof of Theorem 1.3 (using 1-(1-q)^s = q̃ ≤ sq).

Set-monotonicity for `probAux`: if `A ⊆ B` then `probAux U p A ≤ probAux U p B`,

nodes.name: prob_xp_monotone
nodes.docstring:
**Main theorem**: monotonicity of `ProbXp` in `p` on `[0,1]` for upward-closed

nodes.rationale: Monotonicity of ProbXp in p for upward-closed families (stochastic monotonicity of X_p). Standard probability fact used implicitly (X_{q̃} with q̃ ≤ sq) but not stated as a result in the paper.

nodes.name: prob_xp_set_monotone

Set monotonicity of `ProbXp`: if `A ⊆ B` and `0 ≤ q ≤ 1`, then `ProbXp q A ≤ ProbXp q B`.

    Each Bernoulli weight `q^|S| · (1-q)^(|X|-|S|)` is nonnegative when `q ∈ [0,1]`,
    so summing the indicator over a larger set yields a larger value.
nodes.rationale: Generic measure-theoretic plumbing: if A subseteq B then ProbXp q A <= ProbXp q B, because each Bernoulli weight q^|S|(1-q)^(|X|-|S|) is nonnegative. Monotonicity of a probability measure; the paper does not state it as a result. Used by max_w_prob to transfer the event probability along a set inclusion.

nodes.name: q_le_one
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem: q_le_one**
For p ≤ 1, t ≥ 2, and c_sel ≤ 100 * log(2), we have q = (c_sel/100000) * p / log(t) ≤ 1.

**Mathematical Proof**:
- We have (c_sel/100000) * p ≤ c_sel/100000 since p ≤ 1
- For t ≥ 2: log(t) ≥ log(2)
- So q ≤ (c_sel/100000) / log(2)
- If c_sel ≤ 100 * log(2), then (c_sel/100000) / log(2) ≤ (100 * log(2) / 100000) / log(2) = 1/1000 ≤ 1

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: The chosen probability q = (c_sel/100000)·p/log t satisfies q ≤ 1 (for p ≤ 1, t ≥ 2, c_sel ≤ 100·log 2). Parameter well-definedness plumbing ensuring q is a valid probability; not a stated paper result (the specific constants 100000, 100·log 2 are formalization artifacts).

nodes.name: q_pos
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem: q_pos**
For p > 0, c_sel > 0, and t ≥ 2, we have q = (c_sel/100000) * p / log(t) > 0.

**Mathematical Proof**:
- Numerator: (c_sel/100000) * p > 0 since both c_sel > 0 and p > 0
- Denominator: log(t) > 0 for t ≥ 2, since t ≥ 2 > 1 and log is strictly increasing
- Ratio of two positive numbers is positive

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: Positivity of q = (c_sel/100000)·p/log t for p>0, t≥2. A setup/well-definedness fact about the parameter q chosen in the proof of Theorem 1.1; the paper does not state q>0 as a result.

nodes.name: q_prime_le_one
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem: q'_le_one_axiom_final**
Under the same conditions as q'_le_p_div_6, we have q' ≤ 1.

**Proof**: Since p ≤ 1 and q' ≤ p/6 (from q'_le_p_div_6), we have q' ≤ p/6 ≤ 1/6 ≤ 1.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic plumbing in the Proof of Theorem 1.1 establishing q' ≤ 1 so that Theorem 1.3 (which requires a valid probability) applies; q' = 16 s q with q = (c/100000) p/log t. Low confidence: a bookkeeping bound, not a stated result.

nodes.name: q_prime_le_p_div_6
nodes.docstring:
**Theorem: q'_le_p_div_6**
Under the conditions of the main theorem with c_sel ≤ 100 * log(2),
we have q' = 16 * s * q ≤ p/6.

**Mathematical Argument**:
- q = (c_sel/100000) * p / log(t)
- q' = 16 * s * q = 16 * s * (c_sel/100000) * p / log(t)
- For s = ⌈log₂(2t)⌉ ≈ log(2t) / log(2) ≈ log(t) / log(2) + 1 (for large t)
- We can bound: s ≤ log(2t)/log(2) + 1 = 1 + log(t)/log(2) + 1 = 2 + log(t)/log(2)
- So: q' ≤ 16 * (2 + log(t)/log(2)) * (c_sel/100000) * p / log(t)
-     = 16 * c_sel/100000 * p * (2/log(t) + 1/log(2))
- For c_sel ≤ 100 * log(2) and t ≥ 2 (so log(t) ≥ log(2)):
-     q' ≤ 16 * (100*log(2))/100000 * p * (2/log(2) + 1/log(2))
-        = (1600*log(2)/100000) * p * (3/log(2))
-        = (1600/100000) * 3 * p
-        = 4800/100000 * p
-        = 0.048 * p < p/6 ≈ 0.167 * p

**Implementation Note**: This proof requires careful arithmetic with the ceiling bound.
The key insight is that the factor 16 * s * c_sel / (100000 * log t) is bounded by a
small constant (< 1/6) when c_sel ≤ 100 * log 2 and t ≥ 2.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 1, Proof of Main Theorem)
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the parameter inequality q' <= p/6 (equivalently p >= 6q' = 6Cq log t) used near the end of the proof of Theorem 1.1, derived from q = (c_sel/100000) p / log t, q' = 16 s q and the ceiling bound on s = ceil(log_2(2t)). Confidence < 1: this is the concrete constant bookkeeping behind the paper's p >= 6q' assertion with explicit absolute constants chosen in the Lean formalization.

nodes.name: sum_over_subset_le
nodes.docstring:
If Z(W) ≥ ∑_{W' ⊆ H ∩ W} w(W') for all H ∈ ℋ and W, then
    the event {∃ H : ∑_{W' ⊆ H ∩ W} w(W') ≥ 1/2} implies Z(W) ≥ 1/2.

**Source**: @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, Section 4, Proof of Theorem 1.2)
nodes.rationale: ∑_{W'⊆H∩W} w(W') ≤ ∑_{W'⊆W} w(W') since (H∩W).powerset ⊆ W.powerset and w ≥ 0. This realizes the displayed inequality in the proof of Theorem 1.2 dropping the H-restriction (with W = X_{q'}). Low-moderate confidence: a monotonicity step matching one displayed inequality.

nodes.name: membershipReverse
nodes.docstring:
Membership-reversal bijection: a function `W : Fin s → Finset X` is
equivalent to `m : X → Finset (Fin s)` via `m(x) = {i : x ∈ Wᵢ}`.
nodes.rationale: Membership-reversal bijection (Fin s → Finset X) ≃ (X → Finset (Fin s)). Combinatorial plumbing for the per-element factorisation; no paper counterpart.

nodes.name: probXpJoint_singleton
nodes.docstring:
**Lemma B** (per-element factorisation, the deep content).

# References

The underlying probabilistic fact — that the union of `s` independent Bernoulli
random subsets is itself a Bernoulli random subset with parameter
`1 − (1−q)^s` — is a classical result from elementary probability theory and
appears in standard textbook treatments of Bernoulli trials, independence, and
product measures. References:

* M. Mitzenmacher and E. Upfal, *Probability and Computing: Randomization and
  Probabilistic Techniques in Algorithms and Data Analysis*, 2nd ed.,
  Cambridge Univ. Press, 2017. Chapter 1 (basic probability and Bernoulli trials).
* W. Feller, *An Introduction to Probability Theory and Its Applications*,
  Vol. 1, 3rd ed., Wiley, 1968. Chapters on Bernoulli trials and independence.
* G. Grimmett and D. Stirzaker, *Probability and Random Processes*, 3rd ed.,
  Oxford Univ. Press, 2001. Chapter on independence and product spaces.
* N. Alon and J. Spencer, *The Probabilistic Method*, 4th ed., Wiley, 2016.
  Used throughout in the random subset / Erdős–Rényi context (`G(n, p)`).
* S. Janson, T. Łuczak and A. Ruciński, *Random Graphs*, Wiley, 2000.
  Standard treatment of Bernoulli random subsets and their unions.

In the source paper (the application here), this fact is invoked without proof
as the comment "Note that the set `⋃ W_i` has the same distribution as
`X_{q̃}` where `q̃ = 1 − (1 − q)^s`" in §3.3 (line preceding eq. 3.7 of the
selector-process proof).

# Statement

For a fixed subset `S ⊆ X`, the joint probability that `⋃ Wᵢ = S` equals the
Bernoulli weight at parameter `1 - (1-q)^s`:

`ProbXpJoint q s [⋃ W = S] = (1-(1-q)^s)^|S| · ((1-q)^s)^(|X|-|S|)`.

**Proof outline (per-element)**:

1. Apply the `membershipReverse` bijection (defined above): each
   `W : Fin s → Finset X` corresponds to `m : X → Finset (Fin s)` with
   `m(x) = {i : x ∈ Wᵢ}`.

2. Reformulate the joint Bernoulli weight as a per-element product:
   `∏ᵢ q^|Wᵢ|·(1-q)^(|X|-|Wᵢ|) = ∏ₓ q^|m(x)|·(1-q)^(s-|m(x)|)`. Both equal
   `q^N · (1-q)^(s·|X| − N)` where `N = ∑ᵢ |Wᵢ| = ∑ₓ |m(x)|` is the total
   number of pairs `(i, x)` with `x ∈ Wᵢ` (count identity by double counting).

3. Translate the constraint `⋃ Wᵢ = S` to `m ∈ piFinset (T_per_x)` where
   `T_per_x x = if x ∈ S then {T : T ≠ ∅} else {∅}`.

4. Apply `Finset.prod_univ_sum`:
   `∏ₓ ∑_{T ∈ T_per_x x} q^|T|(1-q)^(s-|T|) = ∑_{m ∈ piFinset T_per_x} ∏ₓ ...`

5. Per-element evaluation:
   - `x ∈ S`: `∑_{T ≠ ∅} q^|T|(1-q)^(s-|T|) = (q+(1-q))^s - (1-q)^s = 1-(1-q)^s`
     (via `Fintype.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow` minus the empty term).
   - `x ∉ S`: only `T = ∅` contributes `(1-q)^s`.

6. Combine via `Finset.prod_const` + `Finset.prod_ite` to get
   `(1-(1-q)^s)^|S| · ((1-q)^s)^(|X|-|S|)`.

The full Lean implementation combines the bijection, weight reformulation
(via the per-element decomposition `q^|F|·(1-q)^(|β|-|F|) = ∏ y, if y ∈ F
then q else (1-q)` together with `Finset.prod_comm`), constraint
translation, and per-element evaluation. The required Mathlib pieces
used here are `Fintype.sum_equiv`, `Finset.prod_univ_sum`, and
`Fintype.sum_pow_mul_eq_add_pow`.
nodes.rationale: Per-element Bernoulli factorisation P(⋃W_i = S) = (1-(1-q)^s)^|S| ((1-q)^s)^(|X|-|S|). The classical elementary-probability content behind union_distribution_eq; not stated as a result in the paper.

nodes.name: probXpJoint_sum_swap
nodes.docstring: **Lemma A** (linearity / sum-swap, fully proven).
nodes.rationale: Linearity/sum-swap splitting the joint expectation by the exact union value S. Internal step of the distribution proof; not separately stated in the paper.

nodes.name: union_distribution_eq
nodes.docstring:
**Distribution of `⋃_{i=1}^s W_i` where `W_i ∼ X_q` are independent**
(paper §3.3, the "Note that …" line).

# Proof

Structural, reducing to two helper lemmas:
1. `probXpJoint_sum_swap` (proven) — split by exact union value `S`.
2. `probXpJoint_singleton` (proven) — per-element Bernoulli factorisation.
nodes.rationale: Formalizes the distributional identity that the union ⋃_{i=1}^s W_i of s i.i.d. X_q samples is distributed as X_{q̃} with q̃ = 1-(1-q)^s — exactly the 'Note that …' line in the proof of Theorem 1.2.

nodes.name: main_theorem
nodes.docstring:
Sharp rounding of fractional to integral covers.

This theorem establishes that there exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that:
if a fractional cover w of a hypergraph ℋ satisfies certain cost and support conditions,
then ℋ admits an integral cover with comparably small cost.

Proof strategy (following the paper):
1. Construct weight vectors λ_H for each H ∈ ℋ from the fractional cover w
2. Assume for contradiction that ℋ is not q-small for q = cp/log(t)
3. Apply the Sharp Selector Theorem (Theorem 1.3) to obtain a probabilistic lower bound
4. Derive a lower bound 𝔼[∑_W w(W) · q'^|W|] ≥ 1/6 via λ_H properties
5. Use the cost assumption to show 𝔼[∑_W w(W) · q'^|W|] ≤ 1/12
6. Obtain contradiction: 1/6 ≤ ∑_W w(W) · q'^|W| ≤ 1/12

**Source**: Theorem 1.2 in @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
         (@../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, \ref{thm:main})
nodes.rationale: Direct formalization of Theorem 1.1 (thm:main): existence of c>0 such that a fractional cover w with cost ≤ 1/2 supported on sets of size ≤ t yields IsPSmall ℋ (c·p/log t), i.e. c_int(ℋ;q) ≤ 1/2 for q = cp/log t.

nodes.name: sharp_selector_theorem
nodes.docstring:
Sharp version of Talagrand's selector process conjecture.
    Theorem 1.3 in @../A_sharp_version_of_Talagrands_selector_process_conjecture_and_an_application_to_rounding_fractional_covers.pdf
    (@../../../arXiv-2412.03540v1.tex, \ref{thm:sharp-selector})

Proof strategy:
The deep probabilistic content of the theorem (towers of minimum fragments,
encoding arguments, etc.) is encapsulated by `Workspace.Lemmas.ProbGoodEvent.prob_good_event`,
which gives a `1/3` lower bound on the probability of the heavy event at density
`1 - (1 - q)^s` with `q = 16p`.

To convert this to the desired conclusion at density `16sp`, we use:
- `bernoulli_ineq`: `1 - (1 - q)^s ≤ s · q = 16sp`
- `prob_xp_monotone`: `ProbXp` is monotone in the density for upward-closed events
- The heavy event is upward-closed because `λ_H ≥ 0`, so adding elements to `W`
  only increases the sum `∑_{x ∈ W} λ_H(x)`.
nodes.rationale: Theorem 1.3 (sharp version of Talagrand's selector process conjecture). The Lean statement matches: ∃ c>0, for not-p-small ℋ and weight vectors λ_H in [0,1] supported on H with ∑λ_H ≥ 1, with prob ≥ 1/3 over X_{16sp}, max_H ∑_{x∈X_{16sp}∩H} λ_H(x) ≥ 1-2^{-s}.

nodes.name: FractionalCover
nodes.docstring:
A fractional cover of a family `ℋ ⊆ 2^X` is a function
`w : Finset X → ℝ` taking values in `[0,1]` such that for every `H ∈ ℋ`,
the sum `∑_{W ⊆ H} w(W)` is at least `1`.

This is the LP-relaxation of the cover used to define Talagrand's
fractional expectation threshold.
nodes.rationale: The structure FractionalCover bundles w : Finset X -> R with nonneg, le_one (the [0,1] range), and is_cover (sum_{W subseteq H} w(W) >= 1 for all H in H) -- exactly the paper's definition of a fractional cover. (w_empty is a harmless normalization the paper leaves implicit.)

nodes.name: IntegralCover
nodes.docstring:
An *integral cover* of a family `ℋ ⊆ 2^X` is a `{0,1}`-valued function
`g : Finset X → Bool` such that every `H ∈ ℋ` has some subset `W ⊆ H`
with `g W = true`. Equivalently, the subfamily `{W : g W = true}` meets
every `H ∈ ℋ` in at least one of its subsets.

Only the indicator data and the covering condition are recorded here.
The LP cost bound `∑_W (if g W then 1 else 0) * p^|W| ≤ 1/2` is *not*
part of this structure; it is captured separately by an `IsPSmall`
predicate.
nodes.rationale: The structure records exactly an integral cover: a {0,1}-valued indicator g with the covering condition that every H in ℋ contains a selected subset W. This is the paper's definition of an (integral) cover for ℋ. The LP cost bound is deliberately separated out, as the docstring notes.

nodes.name: IsPSmall
nodes.docstring:
`IsPSmall ℋ p` asserts that the family `ℋ ⊆ 2^X` is *p-small*: there
exists an integral cover `g : 2^X → {0,1}` of `ℋ` whose LP cost
`∑_{W ∈ 2^X} g(W) · p^{|W|}` is at most `1/2`.

This is the central notion `c_int(ℋ; p) ≤ 1/2` from §1 of the paper.
nodes.rationale: IsPSmall ℋ p is defined as the existence of an integral cover g with LP cost ∑_W g(W)·p^|W| ≤ 1/2, i.e. c_int(ℋ;p) ≤ 1/2, which is exactly the paper's definition of 'p-small'. The integral LP objective c_int is defined in eq:int-linprog just above.
